C. Systematically read all 200 files to create a complete function inventory before writing any tests, ensuring the testing plan accounts for everything from the beginning.
D. Start writing tests for the first module alphabetically, using test failures and imports to discover related files organically.
explanation: A. Use Glob and Grep to map codebase structure, identify heavily-coupled modules, create a prioritized plan for high-impact areas, and revise as dependencies are discovered. (Correct) This is the most effective decomposition strategy because it uses lightweight exploration tools first to understand structure and coupling, then prioritizes testing based on impact and dependency density. It is iterative and adapts as new relationships between modules are discovered, which is essential in large, poorly tested codebases. B. Create a fixed testing schedule upfront based on directory structure, allocating equal effort to each top- level directory regardless of code complexity or importance. (Incorrect) This ignores differences in module complexity, risk, and coupling. Treating all directories equally leads to inefficient allocation of testing effort and misses high-risk areas that need deeper coverage. C. Systematically read all 200 files to create a complete function inventory before writing any tests, ensuring the testing plan accounts for everything from the beginning. (Incorrect) While thorough, this is not scalable and delays actual testing work. It front-loads too much analysis and defeats the purpose of incremental discovery, especially in large legacy systems. D. Start writing tests for the first module alphabetically, using test failures and imports to discover related files organically. (Incorrect) This is an unstructured and arbitrary approach. Alphabetical ordering has no relation to system importance or dependency structure, so it risks focusing effort on low-impact areas first and missing critical modules early.

question: Your automated review calls the Claude API for each PR, using tool_use with a report_findings tool that returns a JSON array of finding objects (each with file_path, line_number, severity, category, and description). During testing on a large PR touching 30+ files, the response hits the max_tokens limit and the output is truncated mid-JSON, causing your pipeline's parser to fail. What is the most effective way to handle this?
choices: A. Increase max_tokens to the model's maximum and instruct Claude to keep finding descriptions under 50 words each.
B. Switch from tool_use to prompting Claude to return findings as a markdown list.
C. Split the review into multiple API calls that each analyze a subset of the changed files, then merge the resulting findings arrays.
D. Add retry logic that detects truncated JSON and re-sends the request with instructions to report only critical and high severity findings.
explanation: C. Split the review into multiple API calls that each analyze a subset of the changed files, then merge the resulting findings arrays. Correct Why C is correct: Breaking the PR into smaller batches keeps each JSON response within token limits, preventing truncation and ensuring valid, parseable output. A. Increase max_tokens to the model's maximum and instruct Claude to keep finding descriptions under 50 words each Incorrect May reduce truncation but does not guarantee the response will fit. B. Switch from tool_use to prompting Claude to return findings as a markdown list Incorrect Loses structured output and still does not solve token limit issues. D. Add retry logic that detects truncated JSON and re-sends the request with instructions to report only critical and high severity findings Incorrect Produces incomplete reviews by omitting lower-severity findings.

question: You are setting up a non-interactive automated code review pipeline using Claude Code. You want Claude to analyze a pulled Git diff (git diff) against the main branch and apply a custom set of code review instructions. However, you notice that when you run the pipeline, Claude only looks at the raw diff text itself and completely stops using its file-reading or code navigation tools. As a result, it fails to inspect the broader codebase repository context, which is critical because the diff modifies a core function called by many other external modules. Which change to the CLI invocation will cause Claude to read related files in the repository while still successfully applying your custom review instructions?
choices: A. Replace --system-prompt with --append-system-prompt so your review instructions are added to Claude Code's default prompt instead of overwriting the built-in guidance for using file-reading and code navigation tools.
B. Keep --system-prompt and add --allowedTools "Read, Glob, Grep" so that the non-interactive mode permits file system tools that it otherwise disables.
C. Stop piping the diff via stdin and instead embed the diff contents inside the prompt string, so Claude Code treats the invocation as an agentic session rather than a stream-processing one.
D. Remove --system-prompt entirely and place the review instructions in a CLAUDE.md file at the repo root, since --system-prompt is incompatible with tool use under -p.
explanation: A. Replace --system-prompt with --append-system-prompt so your review instructions are added to Claude Code's default prompt instead of overwriting the built-in guidance for using file-reading and code navigation tools. Correct Why A is correct: --system-prompt replaces Claude Code's default system instructions, which include guidance for using file- reading and code navigation tools. --append-system-prompt preserves those built-in instructions while adding your custom review rules, allowing Claude to inspect related repository files. B. Keep --system-prompt and add --allowedTools "Read, Glob, Grep" Incorrect Tools may be permitted, but replacing the default system prompt can remove the instructions that tell Claude to use them. C. Stop piping the diff via stdin and instead embed the diff contents inside the prompt string Incorrect Changing how the diff is provided does not restore the missing tool-use guidance. D. Remove --system-prompt entirely and place the review instructions in a CLAUDE.md file at the repo root Incorrect --system-prompt is not inherently incompatible with tool use; the issue is overwriting the default prompt.

question: Your development team is using Claude Code to automate test generation across a large codebase. However, developers are frequently rejecting the generated test suites because Claude creates a high volume of trivial assertions or tests that merely maximize line coverage without validating meaningful behavioral logic or edge cases. You want to guide Claude to generate high-quality, production-ready tests directly without introducing high latency or modifying the core pipeline script. Which strategy best ensures that high-quality, meaningful tests are generated in the first place?
choices: A. Restrict test generation to directories where historical quality metrics show higher acceptance rates, disabling it for areas where generated tests consistently require heavy editing.
B. Add post-generation coverage analysis that automatically filters out any generated test that doesn't increase line coverage beyond what existing tests provide.

C. Document testing standards in CLAUDE.md including valuable test criteria, available fixtures with intended use cases, and examples distinguishing meaningful behavioral tests from trivial assertions.
D. Implement a two-phase generation where a second Claude call scores each test against quality criteria, filtering out low-scoring tests before presenting results to developers.
explanation: C. Document testing standards in CLAUDE.md including valuable test criteria, available fixtures with intended use cases, and examples distinguishing meaningful behavioral tests from trivial assertions. Correct Why C is correct: CLAUDE.md provides persistent guidance that shapes test generation from the start. By documenting quality standards, fixtures, and examples of meaningful behavioral tests, Claude is more likely to generate production-ready tests that validate logic and edge cases instead of chasing line coverage. A. Restrict test generation to certain directories Incorrect Limits where tests are generated but does not improve test quality. B. Add post-generation coverage analysis Incorrect Coverage increases do not guarantee meaningful or high-quality tests. D. Implement a second scoring call Incorrect Can filter poor tests but adds latency and modifies the pipeline, which the requirements explicitly avoid.

question: A developer uses Claude Code to refactor a function during their development session. Before committing, they ask the same Claude session to review the code for issues. Later, a separate automated CI review catches several bugs that the same-session review missed. What best explains this discrepancy?
choices: A. The CI environment has access to the full codebase context while the local session only sees the current file
B. The CI review uses a more specific prompt tailored for catching bugs, while the developer's request was too general
C. Claude retains context about its prior reasoning in the session, making it less likely to question its own decisions.
D. The extended session length caused the context window to fill with conversation history, leaving less room for thorough analysis
explanation: C. Claude retains context about its prior reasoning in the session, making it less likely to question its own decisions. Correct Why C is correct: When Claude reviews code in the same session where it created or refactored the code, it retains its earlier reasoning and assumptions. This can lead to confirmation bias, making it less likely to critically re-evaluate its own changes. A fresh CI review starts with no prior attachment to those decisions and may identify issues that the same-session review misses. A. The CI environment has access to the full codebase context while the local session only sees the current file Incorrect Local sessions can also access the codebase using file-reading and navigation tools; this is not the primary reason for the discrepancy. B. The CI review uses a more specific prompt tailored for catching bugs, while the developer's request was too general Incorrect Prompt quality can affect results, but the key issue described is reviewing code within the same session that generated it. D. The extended session length caused the context window to fill with conversation history, leaving less room for thorough analysis Incorrect Long conversations may affect context management, but this is not the main explanation for missing bugs that a fresh review catches.

question: Your automated reviewer uses a single prompt covering security issues, API design, and business logic correctness. Your evaluation suite shows strong recall for API design findings (82%) but poor recall for business logic edge cases in quiz scoring (34%). When you add few-shot examples of logic bugs to the prompt, logic recall improves to 41% but API design recall drops to 68%. How should you address this trade-off to improve detection across both categories?
choices: A. Split the review into separate focused prompts — one for security and API design, another for business logic — each with dedicated examples, then consolidate findings before posting.
B. Replace the few-shot examples with a detailed checklist of specific logic edge cases to verify, such as division-by-zero In score calculations and boundary conditions in grading thresholds.
C. Upgrade to a more capable model tier, since its stronger reasoning will handle both concern types in a single
explanation: A. Split the review into separate focused prompts — one for security and API design, another for business logic — each with dedicated examples, then consolidate findings before posting. Correct Why A is correct: Combining multiple review objectives in a single prompt creates context competition, where adding examples for one category can reduce performance in another. Separate, focused prompts allow each review type to have its own instructions and examples, improving recall across categories without sacrificing performance. B. Replace the few-shot examples with a detailed checklist of specific logic edge cases Incorrect A checklist may help business logic detection but still forces multiple concerns into one prompt and does not eliminate the trade-off. C. Upgrade to a more capable model tier Incorrect A stronger model may improve overall performance, but it does not guarantee removal of prompt interference between different review objectives.

question: Your codebase exploration tool stores session IDs to allow engineers to continue investigations across work sessions. An engineer spent an hour yesterday analyzing a legacy authentication module, building context about its architecture and dependencies. They want to continue today. The session ID is valid, but version control shows 3 of the 12 files the agent previously read were modified overnight by a teammate's merge. What approach best balances efficiency and accuracy?
choices: A. Resume the session and immediately have the agent re-read all 12 previously analyzed files to ensure complete alignment.
B. Resume the session without informing the agent about the changed files, allowing it to naturally detect discrepancies during execution.
C. Resume the session and inform the agent which specific files changed for targeted re-analysis while retaining context on the unchanged files.
D. Start a fresh session to ensure the agent works with current codebase state without stale assumptions from the previous day.
explanation: C. Resume the session and inform the agent which specific files changed for targeted re-analysis while retaining context on the unchanged files. Correct Why C is correct: This approach preserves the valuable context built during the previous session while ensuring accuracy by re- analyzing only the files that changed. It balances efficiency and correctness by avoiding unnecessary re- reading of unchanged files and preventing stale assumptions. A. Resume the session and immediately have the agent re-read all 12 previously analyzed files to ensure complete alignment. Incorrect B. Resume the session without informing the agent about the changed files, allowing it to naturally detect discrepancies during execution. Incorrect Risks relying on outdated assumptions and missing the impact of recent changes. D. Start a fresh session to ensure the agent works with current codebase state without stale assumptions from the previous day. Incorrect Guarantees fresh context but discards an hour of useful analysis and is unnecessarily inefficient.

question: An engineer sees an unfamiliar error message "SYNC_CONFLICT: entity version mismatch detected" in production logs but doesn't know which of the 12 services in the codebase generates it. They ask the agent to help locate the source code. What exploration approach will most efficiently find the responsible code?
choices: A. Use Grep to search for distinctive text from the error message (like "SYNC_CONFLICT" or "entity version mismatch"), then Read the matching files to understand context.
B. Use Glob to find files in directories commonly associated with error handling (such as errors/, exceptions/, or handlers/) across services, then Read each matching file.
C. Use Grep to find all files that import the project's error handling module, then Read those files to locate custom error definitions.
D. Read the project's README and service configuration files to understand the architecture, then systematically Read source files in service directory.
explanation: A. Use Grep to search for distinctive text from the error message (like "SYNC_CONFLICT" or "entity version mismatch"), then Read the matching files to understand context. Correct Why A is correct: Searching for unique strings in the error message is the fastest and most direct way to locate the source code that generates the error. Grep quickly identifies matching files, and Read provides the surrounding context to determine which service is responsible. B. Use Glob to find files in error-related directories Incorrect Error messages may not be defined in dedicated error directories, making this approach inefficient and incomplete. C. Use Grep to find all files that import the project's error handling module Incorrect Many files may import the error module, creating numerous irrelevant matches and increasing investigation time. D. Read the project's README and service configuration files Incorrect Provides architectural context but is a slow, indirect approach for locating a specific error message.

question: You've configured your Claude agent with three MCP servers: one for git operations, one for Jira ticket management, and one for documentation search. When a user asks the agent to "create a branch for JIRA-123 and add documentation links to the ticket," how does the agent access tools across these servers?
choices: A. The agent queries each server sequentially to determine which handles each tool, routing calls based on tool name prefixes.
B. Tools from all configured MCP servers are discovered at connection time and available simultaneously to the agent.
C. You must specify which MCP server to use for each turn, and the agent can only access one server's tools at a time.
D. The agent automatically selects the most relevant server based on the request and loads only that server's tools.
explanation: B. Tools from all configured MCP servers are discovered at connection time and available simultaneously to the agent. Correct Why B is correct: When multiple MCP servers are configured, the agent discovers and loads tools from all connected servers during initialization. It can then use tools across servers in a single request—for example, using the Git server to create a branch, the Jira server to update the ticket, and the Documentation server to retrieve links. A. The agent queries each server sequentially Incorrect The agent does not probe servers one by one for every request or rely on tool name prefixes. C. You must specify which MCP server to use for each turn Incorrect The agent can access tools from multiple servers simultaneously and does not require manual server selection per turn. D. The agent automatically selects one server and loads only that server's tools Incorrect Tools from all configured servers remain available; the agent is not limited to a single server per request.

question: Compliance requires that refunds exceeding $500 must automatically escalate to a human agent—this rule cannot be left to model discretion. Despite clear system prompt instructions, production logs show the agent occasionally processes high-value refunds directly (3% failure rate). How should you achieve guaranteed compliance?
choices: A. Modify the refund tool to return an error message
B. Implement a hook to intercept tool calls when the refund process amount exceeds $500, block it and invoke human escalation.
C. Strengthen the system prompt
D. Add few-shot examples
explanation: B. Implement a hook to intercept tool calls when the refund process amount exceeds $500, block it and invoke human escalation. Correct Why B is correct: Compliance requirements need deterministic enforcement, not model judgment. A hook that intercepts refund tool calls and blocks any refund over $500 guarantees that prohibited actions cannot occur and automatically triggers human escalation. A. Modify the refund tool to return an error message Incorrect An error message depends on the model interpreting and handling it correctly and does not provide guaranteed enforcement. C. Strengthen the system prompt Incorrect Prompts improve behavior but cannot guarantee 100% compliance, as shown by the existing 3% failure rate. D. Add few-shot examples Incorrect Examples may improve adherence but remain probabilistic and cannot enforce a hard compliance rule.

question: Production logs reveal inconsistent error handling: when tool_code fails, the agent sometimes retries 5 times (even if the tool_id doesn't exist), sometimes escalates immediately (premature for temporary network issues), and sometimes adds user-friendly explanation (inappropriate when the issue is a backend permission error). Investigation shows four MCP tool returns uniform error responses: "status": "error", "content": " "type": "Error", "message": "Operation failed." " . The agent learns different types. What's the most effective improvement?
choices: A. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff in your MCP server for all errors, returning to the agent only after retries are exhausted.
B. Create an analyze_error MCP tool the agent calls after any failure to determine the error category and recommended action.
C. Add a few-shot examples to the system prompt demonstrating how to interpret error message patterns and select appropriate responses for each.
D. Enhance error responses with structured metadata. Include error_category (transient/retriable/permission), reason, and a description of what caused the failure.
explanation: D. Enhance error responses with structured metadata. Include error_category (transient/retriable/permission), reason, and a description of what caused the failure. Correct Why D is correct: The current error responses are generic ("Operation failed."), giving the agent no information to distinguish between transient network issues, invalid tool IDs, or permission errors. Structured metadata enables the Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for all errors Incorrect Not all errors are retriable. Retrying permission or invalid-tool errors wastes time and can worsen behavior. Create an analyze_error MCP tool Incorrect Adds extra complexity and latency. The root problem is that the original errors lack sufficient information. Add few-shot examples to the system prompt Incorrect Examples cannot reliably infer error types from identical, generic error messages.

question: Production logs reveal inconsistent error handling. When looking up facts, the agent sometimes retries 5+ times (sadly, when the outer ID doesn't exist), sometimes escalates immediately (prematurely for temporary network issues), and sometimes asks users for clarification (inappropriate when the issue is a backend permission error). Investigation shows your MCP tool returns uniform error responses ("isError": true, "context": "type": "text", "text": "Operation failed." ). The agent cannot distinguish between error types. What's the most effective improvement?
choices: A. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff in your MCP service for all errors returning to the agent only after retries are exhausted.
B. Create an analyze_error MCP tool that the agent calls after any failure to determine the error category and recommended action.
C. Add ten shot examples to the system's conduct_demo training to interpret error message context and select appropriate responses for each.
D. Return structured error metadata in MCP responses.
explanation: D. Return structured error metadata in MCP responses. Correct Why D is correct: The agent receives the same generic error ("Operation failed.") for every failure, so it cannot determine whether it should retry, escalate, or inform the user. Returning structured metadata (for example, error_category, reason, retriable, and permission_denied) enables consistent and appropriate error handling. A. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for all errors Incorrect Not all errors are retriable. Retrying invalid IDs or permission errors wastes time and may cause repeated failures. B. Create an analyze_error MCP tool Incorrect Adds extra complexity and latency. The root issue is insufficient information in the original error response. C. Add ten-shot examples to training Incorrect Examples cannot reliably infer different error types from identical, generic error messages.

question: After expanding the agent's MCP tools with delivery-specific capabilities [apply_promo_code, update_delivery_address, reconcile_delivery], the total tool count has grown from 1 to 7. We have observed that the agent now shows tool selection accuracy has dropped from 86% to 71%. Log analysis reveals the majority of errors involve the agent selecting between semantically overlapping tools — calling issue_credit when process_refund was correct, and calling check_delivery_status when looking order_allready_returns_the_needed_data. Which approach structurally eliminate the semantic overlap identified in the error source?
choices: A. Consolidate semantically overlapping tools – merge issue_credit and process_refund into a single handle_promotions tool with an action parameter and fold check_delivery_status into lookup_order with an optional include_tracking flag.
B. Enable the tool search tool with defer_loading on the six new tools, keeping the original two always loaded, so the agent dynamically discovers specialized tools only when needed.
C. Add few-shot examples to the system prompt demonstrating correct selection for each ambiguous tool, such as showing when issue_credit applies versus when process_refund is appropriate.

D. Split the tools across two sub-agents — a 'financial resolution' agent with issue_credit, process_refund, return_order, and apply_promo_code and a 'delivery operations' agent with the remaining delivery tools — with a coordinating routing between them.
explanation: A. Consolidate semantically overlapping tools – merge issue_credit and process_refund into a single handle_promotions tool with an action parameter and fold check_delivery_status into lookup_order with an optional include_tracking flag. Correct Why A is correct: The primary issue is semantic overlap between tools. When multiple tools perform similar functions or return overlapping information, the agent struggles to choose correctly. Consolidating overlapping tools into unified interfaces removes ambiguity and structurally improves tool selection accuracy. B. Enable tool search with defer_loading Incorrect Reduces the number of simultaneously loaded tools but does not eliminate the underlying semantic overlap. C. Add few-shot examples Incorrect Examples may improve selection temporarily, but they do not address the root cause of overlapping tool capabilities. D. Split tools across two sub-agents Incorrect Domain separation can help organization, but overlap still exists within domains (for example, issue_credit vs. process_refund), so ambiguity remains.

question: You're implementing the escalation logic for when the agent should call a human. Your team processes for different approaches for triggering escalation. Which approach will most reliably identify cases that genuinely B. Configure the agent to escalate after three consecutive tools fails to resolve the customer's stated issue, ensuring a reasonable attempt before involving a human.
choices: A. Instruct the agent to escalate when the customer requests a human, when the issue requires policy exceptions, or when the agent cannot make meaningful progress.
B. Configure the agent to escalate after three consecutive tool failures
C. Build a rules engine that maps issue types, customer segments, and product categories to escalation decisions
D. Implement sentiment analysis that triggers escalation based on frustration indicators
explanation: A. Instruct the agent to escalate when the customer requests a human, when the issue requires policy exceptions, or when the agent cannot make meaningful progress. Correct Why A is correct: This approach directly identifies situations that genuinely require human intervention. It covers customer preference, requests that need policy exceptions or discretionary decisions, and cases where the agent is unable to make meaningful progress. It provides a balanced and reliable escalation strategy. B. Configure the agent to escalate after three consecutive tool failures Incorrect Tool failures do not always mean a human is needed, and some cases require immediate escalation without waiting for multiple failures. C. Build a rules engine that maps issue types, customer segments, and product categories to escalation decisions Incorrect A rigid rules engine is difficult to maintain and cannot capture all situations that require human judgment or customer preference. D. Implement sentiment analysis that triggers escalation based on frustration indicators Incorrect Frustration may indicate dissatisfaction, but it is not a reliable indicator that human intervention is necessary.

question: Your code-review prompts include both implementation changes and the corresponding test file, but the review comments fail to identify untested code paths. The model correctly flags functions that have no tests at all, but it fails to recognize when conditional branches or error-handling paths within tested functions lack coverage. What is the most effective way to improve branch-level gap detection without overcomplicating the pipeline?
choices: A. Interleave the implementation and tests in the prompt, presenting each function immediately before its test cases.
B. Add explicit instructions requiring Claude to enumerate every conditional branch and exception path, then verify that each path has a corresponding test assertion.
C. Implement a two-pass pipeline in which one model call extracts all conditional branches and another cross- references them against test assertions.
D. Include few-shot examples showing code with an uncovered branch and the corresponding review comment identifying the missing test case.
explanation: A. Incorrect Interleaving each function with its tests may improve readability, but it does not specifically teach the model to check whether every conditional branch or exception path is covered by tests. B. Correct Adding explicit instructions to enumerate every conditional branch and exception path, and then verify that each has a corresponding test assertion, directly addresses the branch-level coverage problem. This improves detection of missing tests for if/else branches, early returns, and error-handling paths without adding major pipeline complexity. C. Incorrect A two-pass pipeline can improve accuracy, but it introduces additional orchestration, latency, and cost. The question asks for the most effective improvement without overcomplicating the pipeline. D. Incorrect Few-shot examples can help the model learn the desired behavior, but they are less reliable than giving an explicit branch-checking instruction. The model may still miss branches in unfamiliar code patterns. Final Answer: B

question: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Your automated review jobs take 18 seconds to initialize before Claude begins analyzing code. Profiling reveals that the delay results from automatically discovering hooks, MCP servers, plugins, skills, and multiple nested CLAUDE.md files throughout the monorepo. You need to reduce startup time while ensuring reviews still enforce the coding standards documented in the root- level CLAUDE.md file. What is the most effective approach?
choices: A. Replace the default prompt using --system-prompt-file ./CLAUDE.md, which bypasses default prompt assembly and loads only the project rules.
B. Run in --bare mode and pass --append-system-prompt-file ./CLAUDE.md to load the required project standards explicitly while skipping automatic discovery.
C. Run in --bare mode and repeat all review criteria directly in the -p prompt for every invocation.
D. Keep the default initialization and add --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections to improve prompt-cache reuse across CI runners.
explanation: A. Incorrect — Replace the default prompt entirely Using --system-prompt-file replaces Claude Code’s default system prompt and built-in review behavior. This may remove important coding-assistant instructions and reduce review quality. The goal is to keep the standard behavior while avoiding expensive automatic discovery. B. Correct — Bare mode + append the root CLAUDE.md --bare skips automatic discovery of hooks, MCP servers, plugins, skills, and nested CLAUDE.md files, which is the main source of the 18-second startup delay. Adding --append-system-prompt-file ./CLAUDE.md explicitly loads the root-level coding standards you still want enforced. This gives the best balance of fast startup, preserved default behavior, and consistent project standards. C. Incorrect — Repeat rules in every prompt This avoids discovery overhead, but it duplicates policy text in every invocation, increases maintenance burden, and makes prompts harder to keep consistent with the canonical CLAUDE.md. D. Incorrect — Exclude dynamic sections only This may help prompt-cache reuse, but it does not eliminate the expensive discovery of hooks, MCP servers, plugins, skills, and nested CLAUDE.md files. Startup time would improve far less than with --bare. Final Answer B. Run in --bare mode and pass --append-system-prompt-file ./CLAUDE.md to load the required project standards explicitly while skipping automatic discovery.

question: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. An engineer submits two requests: Request A: “Rename the getUserData function to fetchUserProfile everywhere it’s used.” Request B: “Improve error handling throughout the data processing module—add try/catch blocks, meaningful error messages, and ensure failures don’t silently corrupt data.” For which request does specifying an explicit multi-phase workflow (such as analyze → propose → implement with review) most improve outcome quality?
choices: A. Neither request benefits significantly
B. Request A, the function rename task
C. Both requests benefit equally
D. Request B, the error handling task
explanation: A. Incorrect Neither request benefits significantly Request B is a complex, judgment-heavy change that benefits substantially from a structured workflow. B. Incorrect Request A, the function rename task A global function rename is usually a relatively mechanical refactor. Tools like Grep, language-aware rename features, and tests often make this straightforward. C. Incorrect Both requests benefit equally While both can benefit from planning, the improvement in quality is much greater for Request B. D. Correct Request B, the error handling task Improving error handling requires understanding control flow, identifying failure points, preserving data integrity, avoiding unintended side effects, and designing consistent error messages and recovery behavior. A multi-phase workflow such as analyze → propose → implement → review helps the agent reason about the module before making broad changes, leading to higher-quality and safer results. Final Answer: D

question: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. A developer uses Claude Code to refactor a function during a development session. Before committing, the developer asks the same Claude session to review the code for issues. Later, a separate automated CI review catches several bugs that the same-session review missed. What best explains this discrepancy?
choices: A. Claude retains the implementation context and prior decisions in the session, making it less likely to challenge assumptions underlying its own changes.
B. The session’s context window necessarily became full, leaving insufficient capacity for meaningful review.
C. The CI review must have used a more specific prompt, while the developer’s review request was too general.
D. The CI environment can access the full repository, while a local Claude Code session can access only the current file.
explanation: A. Correct Claude retains the implementation context and prior decisions in the session, making it less likely to challenge assumptions underlying its own changes. When the same Claude session performs both the refactor and the review, it carries forward the reasoning, assumptions, and implementation choices that led to the changes. This can reduce the likelihood of critically questioning those decisions, making the review less independent. B. Incorrect The session’s context window necessarily became full, leaving insufficient capacity for meaningful review. A full context window is not the most likely explanation, and the question does not provide evidence that the context limit was reached. C. Incorrect The CI review must have used a more specific prompt, while the developer’s review request was too general. Prompt quality can affect results, but the key distinction in the scenario is the difference between a same- session self-review and a separate automated review. D. Incorrect The CI environment can access the full repository, while a local Claude Code session can access only the current file. Claude Code can access multiple files and the repository context when used locally; it is not limited to the current file. Final Answer: A

question: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Your pipeline includes a release-notes generation step that classifies and summarizes approximately 200 commits at the end of each weekly release cycle. Each commit is currently sent as a separate Messages API request using a Sonnet-tier Claude model. The release notes are not needed until the following morning, providing approximately 12 hours of acceptable latency. choices: A. Issue the 200 Messages API requests concurrently because parallel execution reduces the per-token price.
B. Submit the 200 requests through the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values and retrieve the results after the batch finishes.
C. Concatenate all 200 commit messages into one Messages API request because reducing the number of requests always reduces token costs.

explanation: A. Incorrect Issue the 200 Messages API requests concurrently because parallel execution reduces the per-token price. Concurrency may reduce total wall-clock time, but it does not reduce the per-token API cost. B. Correct Submit the 200 requests through the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values and retrieve the results after the batch finishes. The Message Batches API is designed for large numbers of independent requests where latency is not critical. It allows you to keep the same model, prompts, and output quality while reducing cost for high-volume asynchronous workloads such as release-note generation. C. Incorrect Concatenate all 200 commit messages into one Messages API request because reducing the number of requests always reduces token costs. Incorrect Replace the Sonnet-tier model with a Haiku-tier model to obtain a lower per-token price. This violates the requirement to retain the same model and preserve output quality. Final Answer: B

question: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JSON schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems. Your extraction system processes two document types: standard monthly reports, which are archived after processing, and urgent exception reports, which must trigger business alerts within 30 minutes of receipt. Both use the same JSON schema. You want to minimize API costs while meeting the latency requirements. How should you architect the processing pipeline?
choices: A. Submit all documents to the Message Batches API with custom_id values for tracking. When results arrive, immediately process urgent documents and trigger delayed alerts for exceptions.
B. Route standard reports to the Message Batches API for 50% cost savings, and route urgent exception reports to the real-time Messages API.
C. Queue all documents and submit hourly batches, flagging urgent documents for expedited handling when batch results return.
D. Submit all documents to the real-time Messages API to ensure consistent processing latency across document types.
explanation: A. Incorrect Submit all documents to the Message Batches API with custom_id values for tracking. When results arrive, immediately process urgent documents and trigger delayed alerts for exceptions. The Message Batches API is asynchronous and does not guarantee the sub-30-minute latency required for urgent exception reports. B. Correct Route standard reports to the Message Batches API for 50% cost savings, and route urgent exception reports to the real-time Messages API. This approach satisfies both requirements: Standard monthly reports: low urgency, so use the lower-cost batch processing path. Urgent exception reports: require alerts within 30 minutes, so use the real-time API. The same JSON schema can be applied in both paths, preserving consistency while optimizing cost. C. Incorrect Queue all documents and submit hourly batches, flagging urgent documents for expedited handling when batch results return. Hourly batching can easily violate the 30-minute alert requirement. D. Incorrect Submit all documents to the real-time Messages API to ensure consistent processing latency across document types. This meets the latency requirement but does not minimize API costs, which is a stated goal. Final Answer: B

question: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems. Testing reveals that when source documents are missing certain specifications, the model fabricates plausible-sounding values to satisfy your schema's required fields. For example, a document mentioning only dimensions receives a fabricated "weight: 2.3 kg" in the extraction output. What schema design change most effectively addresses this hallucination behavior?
choices: A. Add explicit instructions to the prompt stating "only extract information explicitly stated in the document; use placeholder text for missing values."
B. Change fields that may not exist in source documents from required to optional, allowing the model to omit them.
C. Add a "confidence" field alongside each specification where the model self-reports its certainty, then filter out low-confidence extractions.
D. Implement semantic validation that verifies each extracted value appears in or can be inferred from the source document text.
explanation: A. Incorrect Add explicit instructions to the prompt stating “only extract information explicitly stated in the document; use placeholder text for missing values.” Prompt instructions help, but they do not remove the structural pressure created by a schema that requires values for fields that may not exist. B. Correct Change fields that may not exist in source documents from required to optional, allowing the model to omit them. The hallucination occurs because the schema requires a value for every field. Making potentially absent fields optional removes the incentive to fabricate plausible values and allows the extraction to accurately represent missing information. C. Incorrect Add a “confidence” field alongside each specification where the model self-reports its certainty, then filter out low-confidence extractions. Confidence scores are not a reliable mechanism for preventing hallucinations, and fabricated values may still be reported with high confidence. D. Incorrect Implement semantic validation that verifies each extracted value appears in or can be inferred from the source document text. This is a useful downstream safeguard, but it is not the most effective schema design change to prevent the behavior at its source. Final Answer: B

question: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JSON schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems. Your extraction pipeline occasionally receives responses that cannot be parsed as valid JSON, causing downstream processing failures. The current implementation prompts Claude to return JSON in the response text and then parses it. What is the most reliable approach to ensure Claude returns valid, schema-compliant structured data?
choices: A. Add explicit formatting instructions to the prompt with JSON examples, emphasizing that Claude must return only valid JSON with no surrounding text.
B. Use regular expressions to locate and extract JSON from the response text, handling cases where Claude includes explanatory text around the JSON block.
C. Define a tool with a JSON schema specifying the expected structure, using tool use to constrain Claude’s output to schema-compliant JSON.
D. Implement a retry loop that catches JSON parsing errors and re-prompts Claude with the error details, asking it to correct the malformed output.
explanation: A. Incorrect Add explicit formatting instructions to the prompt with JSON examples, emphasizing that Claude must return only valid JSON with no surrounding text. This improves reliability, but the model can still occasionally produce malformed or non-compliant JSON. B. Incorrect Use regular expressions to locate and extract JSON from the response text, handling cases where Claude includes explanatory text around the JSON block. Regex extraction is brittle and does not guarantee schema compliance. C. Correct Define a tool with a JSON schema specifying the expected structure, using tool use to constrain Claude’s output to schema-compliant JSON. Tool use with a JSON schema is the most reliable approach because it constrains the model to return structured arguments that match the defined schema, greatly reducing parsing failures and improving downstream integration. D. Incorrect Implement a retry loop that catches JSON parsing errors and re-prompts Claude with the error details, asking it to correct the malformed output. Retries can recover from some failures, but they add latency, cost, and complexity and are less reliable than schema-constrained tool output. Final Answer: C

question: You are building developer-productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools—Read, Write, Bash, Grep, and Glob—and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Your productivity agent connects to three MCP servers: an issue tracker with search_issues , get_issue , and create_comment ; a documentation wiki with search_docs , get_page , and list_spaces ; and a database explorer with run_query , get_schema , and list_databases . For cross-system questions such as, “Which database tables are affected by the authentication refactor in PROJ-1234?”, the agent makes eight to ten sequential exploratory calls, lacks visibility into each server’s available content, and exhausts context before completing complex investigations. What architectural change best leverages MCP capabilities to address these problems?
choices: A. Add a prepare_investigation tool to each server that accepts a natural-language question and returns relevant summaries.
B. Consolidate all three systems into one unified MCP server with cross-referencing capabilities.
C. Expose each server’s content catalog as MCP resources, including issue summaries, documentation hierarchies, and database schemas.
D. Add an orchestrator that routes each question to one server based on keywords.
explanation: A. Incorrect Add a prepare_investigation tool to each server that accepts a natural-language question and returns relevant summaries. This may reduce some calls, but it does not solve the core problem of discoverability and context-efficient exploration across systems. B. Incorrect Consolidate all three systems into one unified MCP server with cross-referencing capabilities. This is a heavy operational change and is not necessary to take advantage of MCP’s native strengths. C. Correct Expose each server’s content catalog as MCP resources, including issue summaries, documentation hierarchies, and database schemas. MCP resources are designed for discoverable, structured context. Exposing issue summaries, wiki structure, and database schemas allows the agent to understand what content exists before making targeted tool calls, reducing exploratory requests and preserving context for complex investigations. D. Incorrect Add an orchestrator that routes each question to one server based on keywords. Cross-system questions inherently require information from multiple servers, so single-server routing would miss important relationships. Final Answer: C

question: The coordinator provides detailed step-by-step instructions to the web-search subagent, specifying exact search queries, source priorities, and date filters. Production monitoring reveals three issues: (1) the subagent reports “insufficient results” instead of trying alternative approaches when the specified searches fail, (2) research quality drops for emerging topics that do not match expected patterns, and (3) the subagent rarely surfaces valuable tangential sources. What is the most effective way to improve subagent adaptability?
choices: A. Specify research objectives and quality criteria—such as coverage breadth, source diversity, and recency— rather than prescribing procedural steps, allowing the subagent to determine its search strategy.
B. Remove procedural details entirely and delegate using simple goals such as “research this topic thoroughly,” relying on the subagent’s general capabilities.
C. Add fallback directives requiring alternative query formulations whenever the specified searches produce fewer than a predetermined number of results.
D. Classify each topic as either “well-defined” or “exploratory” and use a different instruction style for each category.
explanation: A. Correct Specify research objectives and quality criteria—such as coverage breadth, source diversity, and recency—rather than prescribing procedural steps, allowing the subagent to determine its search strategy. This directly addresses all three problems: The subagent can adapt when initial searches fail. It can explore emerging topics that do not fit predefined query patterns. It is encouraged to surface valuable tangential sources through broader, goal-oriented exploration. B. Incorrect Remove procedural details entirely and delegate using simple goals such as “research this topic thoroughly,” relying on the subagent’s general capabilities. This gives too little guidance and may reduce consistency and quality control. Incorrect Add fallback directives requiring alternative query formulations whenever the specified searches produce fewer than a predetermined number of results. Incorrect Classify each topic as either “well-defined” or “exploratory” and use a different instruction style for each category. This can help in some cases, but it is less effective than shifting from procedural control to objective-based delegation across all research tasks. Final Answer: A

question: The synthesis agent completes its initial pass but flags that three key research questions remain unanswered because the web-search and document-analysis agents did not find relevant information on those specific subtopics. The coordinator currently proceeds directly to report generation, producing reports with incomplete coverage. What change would most effectively improve research completeness?
choices: A. Have the coordinator evaluate the synthesis output for gaps, then redelegate targeted queries to the web- search and document-analysis agents before invoking synthesis again.
B. Have the report-generation agent identify unanswered research questions so users understand the limitations of the final output.
C. Increase the initial breadth of queries sent to the web-search and document-analysis agents to reduce the probability of missing relevant information.
D. Give the synthesis agent direct access to web-search tools so it can autonomously fill knowledge gaps without returning control to the coordinator.
explanation: A. Correct Have the coordinator evaluate the synthesis output for gaps, then redelegate targeted queries to the web-search and document-analysis agents before invoking synthesis again. This creates an iterative research loop: synthesize → identify gaps → perform targeted follow-up research → resynthesize. It directly improves completeness while preserving clear separation of responsibilities between coordinator, retrieval agents, and synthesis. B. Incorrect Have the report-generation agent identify unanswered research questions so users understand the limitations of the final output. This improves transparency but does not improve research completeness. C. Incorrect Increase the initial breadth of queries sent to the web-search and document-analysis agents to reduce the probability of missing relevant information. Broader initial searches may help somewhat, but they increase cost and noise and still cannot guarantee coverage of specific missing subtopics. D. Incorrect Give the synthesis agent direct access to web-search tools so it can autonomously fill knowledge gaps without returning control to the coordinator. This blurs responsibilities and reduces orchestration control. Coordinators are better suited to managing iterative retrieval and synthesis workflows. Final Answer: A

question: In addition to your CI pipeline, your organization has enabled Claude’s managed Code Review through the Claude GitHub App on this repository, and reviews run automatically on every pull request. Reviews average 18 findings per pull request. Developer feedback reveals three categories of unwanted noise: (1) style and formatting issues already enforced by your CI linter, (2) findings on automatically generated template code under src/gen/*, and (3) rendering-helper patterns that are intentional project conventions but are flagged because they resemble common anti-patterns. Only approximately four findings per pull request are genuine logic bugs. What is the most effective way to reduce this noise while preserving the detection of real issues?
choices: A. Create a REVIEW.md file at the repository root containing skip rules for CI-enforced checks and generated files, together with a verification requirement that rendering-related findings cite a specific line demonstrating incorrect behavior.

B. Configure separate GitHub Actions workflow files for each code area: one for generated code with findings suppressed, one for rendering code with custom instructions, and one general workflow for everything else.

C. Add custom review instructions to a GitHub Actions workflow file, using the action’s prompt parameter to suppress duplicate lint findings, ignore generated template code, and impose stricter evidence requirements on rendering-related issues.
D. Add detailed explanations to the project’s CLAUDE.md describing intentional patterns, stating that CI handles linting, and identifying src/gen/ as automatically generated code.
explanation: A. Correct Create a REVIEW.md file at the repository root containing skip rules for CI-enforced checks and generated files, together with a verification requirement that rendering-related findings cite a specific line demonstrating incorrect behavior. This is the most effective option because it gives the managed review system review-specific instructions: ignore issues already enforced by CI, skip generated code under src/gen/*, and require stronger evidence before flagging intentional rendering patterns. These targeted review constraints reduce noise while preserving detection of real logic bugs. B. Incorrect Configure separate GitHub Actions workflow files for each code area: one for generated code with findings suppressed, one for rendering code with custom instructions, and one general workflow for everything else. This adds workflow complexity and does not directly control the behavior of the managed code review system. C. Incorrect Add custom review instructions to a GitHub Actions workflow file, using the action’s prompt parameter to suppress duplicate lint findings, ignore generated template code, and impose stricter evidence requirements on rendering-related issues. This applies to a workflow-based review integration, not the managed review configuration described in the question. D. Incorrect Add detailed explanations to the project’s CLAUDE.md describing intentional patterns, CLAUDE.md provides general repository guidance, but it is less precise for controlling review-time suppression and evidence requirements than a dedicated review-configuration file. Final Answer: A

question: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution. Your team has connected a custom MCP server that provides DevOps workflow templates. The server exposes several MCP prompts (such as deploy_checklist and incident_response ) in addition to tools. How do these MCP prompts become accessible within Claude Code?
choices: A. They are automatically prepended to every conversation as additional system-level context, influencing Claude’s behavior throughout the session.
B. They are added to Claude Code’s tool registry alongside the server’s tools, invoked automatically by the model when relevant to the task.
C. They are surfaced as @ -mentionable resources alongside files, fetched and attached to your message when referenced.
D. They appear as slash commands (e.g., /mcp servername deploy_checklist ) that you can invoke, with arguments passed after the command name.

MCP prompts are not injected automatically into every conversation. B. Incorrect They are added to Claude Code’s tool registry alongside the server’s tools, invoked automatically by the model when relevant to the task. Correct They appear as slash commands (e.g., /mcp__servername__deploy_checklist) that you can invoke, with arguments passed after the command name. In Claude Code, MCP prompts are exposed as slash commands. You invoke them explicitly, and any arguments are provided after the command name. Final Answer: D

question: Your pipeline includes a release-notes generation step that classifies and summarizes approximately 200 commits at the end of each weekly release cycle. Each commit is currently sent as a separate Messages API call using a Sonnet-tier Claude model. The release notes are not needed until the following morning, so results have approximately 12 hours of acceptable latency. Which approach satisfies all these constraints?

B. Issue the 200 Messages API requests in parallel using concurrent connections, because concurrency lowers the per-token price charged by the API.
C. Submit the 200 requests to the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values and retrieve the results after the batch finishes, which applies a 50% discount to all input and output tokens.

explanation: A. Incorrect Concatenate all 200 commit messages into a single Messages API request and have the model return all summaries in one response, because fewer requests always reduce total token cost. Fewer requests do not guarantee lower token usage. Combining all commits can increase context complexity, reduce output quality, and may use a similar or larger number of tokens overall. B. Incorrect Issue the 200 Messages API requests in parallel using concurrent connections, because concurrency lowers the per-token price charged by the API. Concurrency can reduce total processing time, but it does not change the per-token pricing. C. Correct Submit the 200 requests to the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values and retrieve the results after the batch finishes, which applies a 50% discount to all input and output tokens. The Message Batches API is designed for large asynchronous workloads where latency is not critical. It preserves the same model, prompts, and output quality while reducing cost through the batch pricing discount. D. Incorrect Switch the summarization calls from the Sonnet-tier model to a Haiku-tier model to take advantage of Haiku’s lower per-token rates. This violates the requirement to keep the same model tier and maintain the same output quality. Final Answer: C

question: You are building developer-productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools—Read, Write, Bash, Grep, and Glob—and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) Engineers frequently ask the agent to cross-reference code changes with Jira tickets during reviews—checking ticket descriptions, acceptance criteria, and recent comments. This currently requires manually copying and pasting content into conversations. The team wants the agent to access this standard Jira ticket data directly.
choices: A. Use the Bash tool with curl to call Jira’s REST API, including authentication headers and parsing JSON responses inline.
B. Build a custom MCP server wrapping Jira’s API with tools designed specifically for this team’s code-review workflow.

explanation: A. Incorrect Use the Bash tool with curl to call Jira’s REST API, including authentication headers and parsing JSON responses inline. This works, but it is brittle, requires manual authentication handling, and does not provide discoverable, reusable interfaces for the team. B. Incorrect Build a custom MCP server wrapping Jira’s API with tools designed specifically for this team’s code-review workflow. Correct Integrate an existing Jira MCP server that exposes tickets, comments, and metadata through discoverable tool interfaces. This is the best fit for the Agent SDK and MCP architecture. It provides structured, discoverable access to Jira data, avoids manual copy/paste, and enables the agent to retrieve ticket descriptions, acceptance criteria, comments, and metadata directly during code reviews. Final Answer: D

question: A user expands the research system beyond its original web-search agent by adding specialized data sources. A financial API agent returns structured JSON containing revenue, margins, and growth rates. A news-monitoring agent returns prose summaries of recent developments. A patent-analysis agent returns structured lists of technology areas. The synthesis agent combines these results into executive briefings. Currently, it converts everything into bullet points, causing financial comparisons to lose tabular clarity and news summaries to lose their narrative flow. What change would most improve briefing quality?
choices: A. Standardize all subagent outputs as prose summaries with inline citations.
B. Standardize all subagent outputs as JSON containing fields for claim, evidence, source, and confidence.
C. Update the synthesis agent to render each content type appropriately—financial data as tables, news as prose, and technology areas as structured lists.
D. Add a format-conversion layer that transforms every subagent result into a common intermediate representation before synthesis.
explanation: A. Incorrect Standardize all subagent outputs as prose summaries with inline citations. This would reduce the clarity of structured financial data and technology lists. B. Incorrect Standardize all subagent outputs as JSON containing fields for claim, evidence, source, and confidence. Useful for validation and traceability, but it does not solve the presentation-quality problem in executive briefings. C. Correct Update the synthesis agent to render each content type appropriately—financial data as tables, news as prose, and technology areas as structured lists. Different information types have different optimal representations: Financial data: tables for comparison News: narrative prose for flow and context Technology areas: structured lists for scanability Adapting rendering to content type preserves the strengths of each source and produces higher-quality executive briefings. D. Incorrect Add a format-conversion layer that transforms every subagent result into a common intermediate representation before synthesis. A common internal representation may help orchestration, but it does not inherently improve the final presentation quality. Final Answer: C

question: Users report that final reports sometimes lack depth on specific subtopics. Investigation shows that the document- analysis agent frequently identifies evidence gaps—for example, noting that “the retrieved sources discuss API authentication but lack details about token-refresh patterns.” Under the current strict pipeline, this insight is not actionable because searching has already finished. What is the most effective architectural change?
choices: A. Add a research-planning agent before the initial search phase to decompose every topic into detailed subquestions.
B. Have the synthesis agent assign confidence scores to each report section and flag insufficiently supported sections for manual review.
C. Require the analysis agent to return specific evidence gaps to the coordinator, which launches targeted searches and invokes analysis again until the defined coverage criteria are satisfied
D. Have the coordinator look for general gap indicators in the analysis output and run additional searches without repeating the analysis stage.
explanation: A. Incorrect Add a research-planning agent before the initial search phase to decompose every topic into detailed subquestions. This improves initial coverage but cannot address new evidence gaps discovered during analysis. B. Incorrect Have the synthesis agent assign confidence scores to each report section and flag insufficiently supported sections for manual review. This increases transparency but does not automatically improve report depth. C. Correct Require the analysis agent to return specific evidence gaps to the coordinator, which launches targeted searches and invokes analysis again until the defined coverage criteria are satisfied. This creates a closed-loop iterative research architecture: analyze retrieved evidence, identify precise missing information, perform targeted follow-up searches, reanalyze, repeat until coverage requirements are met. It directly converts analysis insights into actionable retrieval. D. Incorrect Have the coordinator look for general gap indicators in the analysis output and run additional searches without repeating the analysis stage. Without reanalysis, the system cannot determine whether the new evidence actually resolves the identified gaps. Final Answer: C

question: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high- ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools ( get_customer , lookup_order , process_refund , escalate_to_human ). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate. Your process_refund tool returns two types of errors: technical errors (“503 Service Unavailable”, “Connection timeout”) that are transient (~5% of calls), and business errors (“Order exceeds 30-day return window”, “Item already refunded”) that are permanent (~12% of calls). Monitoring shows the agent wastes 3–4 turns retrying business errors that can never succeed. Currently, both error types return only a plain text message to Claude. What’s the most effective way to reduce wasted retries while improving customer-facing response quality?
choices: A. Implement automatic retry logic at the tool layer for technical errors only, passing business errors to Claude without retries.
B. Add few-shot examples showing how to distinguish retriable from non-retriable errors by parsing error message text.
C. Add a check_refund_eligibility tool that must be called before process_refund to prevent business rule violations.
D. Return structured error responses with " retriable " : false for business errors and a customer-friendly explanation for Claude to use.
explanation: A. Incorrect Implement automatic retry logic at the tool layer for technical errors only, passing business errors to Claude without retries. This helps with transient failures, but Claude still receives unstructured business-error text and may continue retrying unnecessarily. B. Incorrect Add few-shot examples showing how to distinguish retriable from non-retriable errors by parsing error message text. Parsing free-form error text is brittle and less reliable than explicit machine-readable metadata. C. Incorrect Add a check_refund_eligibility tool that must be called before process_refund to prevent business rule violations. This may reduce some business errors, but it adds an extra call to every refund request and does not solve the general problem of distinguishing retriable and non-retriable failures. D. Correct Return structured error responses with "retriable": false for business errors and a customer- friendly explanation for Claude to use. Structured errors give the agent explicit control-flow information: Technical errors: retriable: true Business errors: retriable: false Including a customer-friendly explanation allows Claude to respond clearly and empathetically without wasting turns on impossible retries. Final Answer: D

question: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. During initial testing of the automated review pipeline, you notice that reviews on large pull requests containing more than 50 changed files sometimes take over 20 minutes and cost $8–$12 per run because of extensive agentic loops. Claude reads files, runs analysis tools, and iterates many times. Your team needs each invocation to abort once it reaches both a fixed iteration count and a fixed dollar amount, enforced by Claude Code itself rather than by the surrounding job runner. Which configuration change directly enforces both per-invocation caps?
choices: A. Switch the --model flag to a smaller, less expensive model so each iteration uses fewer tokens and has a lower per-call cost.
B. Set timeout-minutes: 5 on the GitHub Actions job step and monitor per-run costs through the Anthropic Console usage dashboard.
C. Add --max-turns 10 --max-budget-usd 2.00 to the claude -p invocation to cap iterations and spending.
D. Set --permission-mode dontAsk to automatically deny tool-permission requests not included in the explicitly allowed set.
explanation: A. Incorrect Switch the --model flag to a smaller, less expensive model so each iteration uses fewer tokens and has a lower per-call cost. question: Your schema includes a 'skills: string[] field. explanation: A. Correct Add few-shot examples demonstrating compound phrase handling, explicit mention criteria, and appropriate entry granularity.
